title: I Let the Book-Club Host Keep the Spoilers Rule She Broke First

parts.text: I arrived at 7:00 with page 312 in my head because the host, Corinne, had emailed NO SPOILERS PAST THE WEEKLY MARKER. Then she announced the ending while pouring pinot. I was thirty, holding a paperback with a grocery receipt as a bookmark. Two members gasped. Corinne said if you were behind that's on you. I had read on the marker. She had not. I posted the email in the group chat with the timestamp of her announcement. Then she texted me privately: don't make this a thing, it's my house.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: She wants the house to outrank the email she sent.

social.video_title: She emailed a spoiler ban and poured the ending — Part 1/2
social.description: Page 312, pinot, grocery-receipt bookmark. The host was behind and still talking. Would you have stayed for dessert?

parts.text: I made it a thing by suggesting we rotate hosts. We did. Corinne skipped a month. The book stayed surprising for people who followed her own marker. I ate store cookies at someone else's table. The paperback survived. Private texts about houses do not overwrite group emails. The ending will wait. That is what endings do when you let them.

social.video_title: The club rotated off the pinot pulpit — Part 2/2
social.description: New table, intact ending, cookies. Was a house a spoiler pass?
